html:
The Dja Dja Wurrung, who call themselves Djaara, are an Aboriginal people of central Victoria, around the Loddon and Avoca rivers and present day Bendigo and Castlemaine. They are one of the peoples of the Kulin alliance.

Like other Kulin, they have two moieties, named for the creator spirits Bunjil the eagle and Waa the crow, and are made up of about sixteen clans. Neighbours included the Taungurung to the east, the Djab Wurrung to the west and the Wurundjeri to the southeast.

Squatters took up their land from the late 1830s, and conflict, massacres and above all disease cut their numbers sharply. A government protectorate station was set up for them at Mount Franklin in 1841. Then in 1851 gold was found at Bendigo and Castlemaine, and the Victorian gold rush filled their country with diggers. In 2013 the Dja Dja Wurrung signed a settlement with the state of Victoria recognising them as traditional owners. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
